Sections.Name: Access and Registration
Sections.Introduction: The following supplied captures illustrate the access and registration and their visible controls.

Sections.Name: Administrator Interfaces
Sections.Introduction: The following supplied captures illustrate the administrator interfaces and their visible controls.

Sections.Name: Staff Interfaces
Sections.Introduction: The following supplied captures illustrate the staff interfaces and their visible controls.

Sections.Name: Member Interfaces
Sections.Introduction: The following supplied captures illustrate the member interfaces and their visible controls.

Figures.Title: Shared Sign-in Interface
Figures.Caption: Figure 6. Shared Sign-in Interface
Figures.Description: The shared sign-in page provides email and password inputs, Remember my login, password recovery, and online membership registration. The appearance control changes the displayed theme. Access after authentication depends on the account role and applicable browser approval.

Figures.Title: Password Recovery Request
Figures.Caption: Figure 7. Password Recovery Request
Figures.Description: The password-recovery dialog collects the email linked to the account and provides Send Reset Link and Cancel actions. This capture shows the request form before the result message.

Figures.Title: Password Recovery Response
Figures.Caption: Figure 8. Password Recovery Response
Figures.Description: The recovery dialog displays a conditional message advising the user to check the inbox and spam folder if an account uses the supplied email. This message avoids confirming whether the account exists; it does not establish delivery of a reset email.

Figures.Title: Online Membership Registration
Figures.Caption: Figure 9. Online Membership Registration
Figures.Description: The complete supplied registration capture shows personal and emergency-contact details, plan and date choices, health declarations, fitness goals, agreements, signature, and portal credentials. Submission requests membership review rather than immediate membership activation or online payment.

Figures.Title: Application Receipt and Email Confirmation
Figures.Caption: Figure 10. Application Receipt and Email Confirmation
Figures.Description: The receipt displays the submitted application reference, requested plan, amount, email, and Pending review status. Its instructions distinguish confirming the sign-in email from the subsequent staff or administrator membership decision.

Figures.Title: Administrator Dashboard
Figures.Caption: Figure 11. Administrator Dashboard
Figures.Description: The dashboard brings together registration requests, membership and sales summary cards, low-stock alerts, and current-day attendance. These displayed values describe the captured state and are not measured system performance results.

Figures.Title: Administrator Registration Review
Figures.Caption: Figure 12. Administrator Registration Review
Figures.Description: The Approvals view expands a pending registration to show submitted details and signature with Reject and Approve & Create Account actions. The operator reviews the request and applicable in-person payment before completing the authorized decision.

Figures.Title: Active Membership Records
Figures.Caption: Figure 13. Active Membership Records
Figures.Description: The active-membership list provides search, plan filters, and individual Change Plan, Renew, and Show actions. The list supports membership administration within the permitted workflow.

Figures.Title: Expired Membership Records
Figures.Caption: Figure 14. Expired Membership Records
Figures.Description: The Expired tab provides search and plan filters for lapsed memberships. The captured empty state indicates no matching records in this view, rather than an absence of expired memberships in every environment.

Figures.Title: Administrator Walk-in Registration
Figures.Caption: Figure 15. Administrator Walk-in Registration
Figures.Description: The complete supplied Add New Member dialog collects separate name inputs, personal and emergency-contact details, plan information, declarations, signature, and portal credentials. The operator submits the completed walk-in registration using the available counter action.

Figures.Title: Administrator QR Attendance Workspace
Figures.Caption: Figure 16. Administrator QR Attendance Workspace
Figures.Description: The attendance workspace provides the member QR scanning entry point, phone-connection status, paired-camera controls, date selection, and attendance log. The capture shows the workspace before a new scan result.

Figures.Title: Attendance Camera Selection
Figures.Caption: Figure 17. Attendance Camera Selection
Figures.Description: Choose a Camera offers This device and Phone camera. The dialog states the pairing duration and setup-code time limit shown by the interface; selecting a source begins the corresponding camera workflow.

Figures.Title: Phone-Camera Connection and Pairing Management
Figures.Caption: Figure 18. Phone-Camera Connection and Pairing Management
Figures.Description: The connection dialog shows a setup QR, visibility control, scanner link, phone limit, paired phones, and pending QR reservations. End pairing and End QR manage distinct connection states, while closing the window is a separate action. The pictured setup code belongs to the captured session.

Figures.Title: Attendance Scanner Sign-in
Figures.Caption: Figure 19. Attendance Scanner Sign-in
Figures.Description: The scanner page requires operator username and password and offers installation of the attendance app. Authentication precedes scanning; this sign-in capture does not demonstrate camera permission or a completed physical scan.

Figures.Title: Administrator Inventory Catalog
Figures.Caption: Figure 20. Administrator Inventory Catalog
Figures.Description: The inventory catalog displays product images, configured prices, sale units, stock quantities, and maintenance controls. Supplements and merchandise appear in their catalog groups. Inventory modification remains an administrator task.

Figures.Title: Inventory Stock Filter
Figures.Caption: Figure 21. Inventory Stock Filter
Figures.Description: The stock-status filter offers All products, Low stock, Out of stock, and In stock. Selecting a status narrows the displayed catalog without changing the underlying stock.

Figures.Title: Membership Sales Monitoring
Figures.Caption: Figure 22. Membership Sales Monitoring
Figures.Description: The Membership sales tab shows overall income, membership totals, period controls, and transaction rows. The figures are captured sample records; they do not establish independently audited revenue.

Figures.Title: Product Sales Monitoring
Figures.Caption: Figure 23. Product Sales Monitoring
Figures.Description: The Products sales tab shows daily product income, period selection, and sales records. The empty table in this capture is specific to the selected period.

Figures.Title: Administrator Product Sale Entry
Figures.Caption: Figure 24. Administrator Product Sale Entry
Figures.Description: The New Sale dialog collects customer name, product, amount, and sale unit and displays the computed total and available stock. Complete submits the transaction; the capture itself does not show a successful stock deduction.

Figures.Title: Administrator Report Selection
Figures.Caption: Figure 25. Administrator Report Selection
Figures.Description: The Reports workspace groups membership, daily operations, payments, and sales reports. Area and period filters define the requested report selection before export or printing.

Figures.Title: Report Area Filter
Figures.Caption: Figure 26. Report Area Filter
Figures.Description: The report-area menu includes membership, member status, renewals, archives, attendance, inventory, payments, and sales. This supplied detail documents the available report categories.

Figures.Title: Report Period Filter
Figures.Caption: Figure 27. Report Period Filter
Figures.Description: The period menu offers Specific day, Date range, and Full year. The selected period determines the time scope of the requested report.

Figures.Title: Report Export and Printing Actions
Figures.Caption: Figure 28. Report Export and Printing Actions
Figures.Description: The supplied action detail shows Export PDFs as ZIP and Print selected. These controls describe output options and do not show a generated archive or completed print job.

Figures.Title: Staff Directory Search
Figures.Caption: Figure 29. Staff Directory Search
Figures.Description: The staff directory supports searching by name, username, or email and provides Details and Deactivate actions. Its displayed account states support administrator account management.

Figures.Title: Staff Accounts in Light Appearance
Figures.Caption: Figure 30. Staff Accounts in Light Appearance
Figures.Description: The light-theme capture shows the staff-account creation form and searchable directory alongside the account menu. Appearance choices affect presentation while the account-management task remains the same.

Figures.Title: Staff Account Creation in Dark Appearance
Figures.Caption: Figure 31. Staff Account Creation in Dark Appearance
Figures.Description: The dark-theme Staff Accounts page shows separate name fields, assigned credentials, contact information, password confirmation, and the staff directory. Creating a staff account is distinct from registering a member.

Figures.Title: Forget Trusted Administrator Browser
Figures.Caption: Figure 32. Forget Trusted Administrator Browser
Figures.Description: The confirmation explains that forgetting the browser revokes its administrator trust and ends its dashboard and scanner sessions. The destructive confirmation is separate from ordinary logout and requires verification again at a later sign-in.

Figures.Title: Administrator Activity Logs
Figures.Caption: Figure 33. Administrator Activity Logs
Figures.Description: The activity viewer provides filters, readable event rows, timestamps, actor and category information, and expandable details. It supports reviewing recorded actions; opening an event does not execute that action.

Figures.Title: Activity Log Action Filter
Figures.Caption: Figure 34. Activity Log Action Filter
Figures.Description: The action menu exposes event-specific choices, including account, attendance, browser approval, and session events. It narrows the displayed audit entries to the chosen action.

Figures.Title: Activity Log Category Filter
Figures.Caption: Figure 35. Activity Log Category Filter
Figures.Description: The category menu groups membership, attendance, inventory, sales, accounts, security, sessions, phone pairings, and reports. These categories help locate relevant recorded events.

Figures.Title: Administrator Logout Confirmation
Figures.Caption: Figure 36. Administrator Logout Confirmation
Figures.Description: The ordinary logout dialog explains that this browser stays trusted. Cancel returns to the session, while Log out confirms sign-out without using the separate forget-browser action.

Figures.Title: Staff Dashboard and Attendance History
Figures.Caption: Figure 37. Staff Dashboard and Attendance History
Figures.Description: The staff dashboard groups Attendance, Product sales, Membership, and Request approval tasks. The attendance view places check-in/check-out controls beside visit history, including the statuses visible in this capture.

Figures.Title: Staff QR Attendance Controls
Figures.Caption: Figure 38. Staff QR Attendance Controls
Figures.Description: The attendance panel offers camera scanning and a manual lookup using member QR, name, or Gmail. An authorized attendance operation determines the applicable check-in or check-out state.

Figures.Title: Staff Attendance Lookup Detail
Figures.Caption: Figure 39. Staff Attendance Lookup Detail
Figures.Description: This second supplied attendance view shows the member-lookup input and Find member action beneath camera scanning. It documents the highlighted input state without demonstrating a completed lookup or visit transaction.

Figures.Title: Staff Product-Sale Workspace
Figures.Caption: Figure 40. Staff Product-Sale Workspace
Figures.Description: The complete staff sales capture combines customer and product inputs, quantity and unit controls, recent own sales, and the permitted product catalog. Staff sales access does not grant inventory maintenance.

Figures.Title: Staff Product Selection
Figures.Caption: Figure 41. Staff Product Selection
Figures.Description: The product menu lists merchandise and supplement choices with configured prices and units. The chosen product determines the applicable sale entry rather than a single unit shared by every item.

Figures.Title: Staff Walk-in Membership Services
Figures.Caption: Figure 42. Staff Walk-in Membership Services
Figures.Description: The Membership workspace separates Add Member, Renewal, and Change Plan. The add-member form collects personal and emergency-contact details, portal credentials, a standard plan, and signature before Create member & record payment.

Figures.Title: Staff Membership Plan Choices
Figures.Caption: Figure 43. Staff Membership Plan Choices
Figures.Description: The supplied plan menu shows monthly, half-month, and walk-in options with their displayed prices and durations. These are captured choices rather than a guarantee that future plan configuration will remain identical.

Figures.Title: Staff Request Approval Workspace
Figures.Caption: Figure 44. Staff Request Approval Workspace
Figures.Description: The request-review page displays pending online requests with available approval and rejection actions. Staff review membership requests through this workflow rather than activating them merely by opening the page.

Figures.Title: Staff Request Type Filter
Figures.Caption: Figure 45. Staff Request Type Filter
Figures.Description: The request filter offers All requests, Registration, and Renewal. It separates the pending request types within the authorized review workspace.

Figures.Title: Staff Account Menu in Dark Appearance
Figures.Caption: Figure 46. Staff Account Menu in Dark Appearance
Figures.Description: The staff account menu offers Light mode, Dark mode, and Logout. The selected dark appearance is a display preference.

Figures.Title: Staff Account Menu in Light Appearance
Figures.Caption: Figure 47. Staff Account Menu in Light Appearance
Figures.Description: The corresponding light-theme capture shows the same appearance and logout actions. These settings do not change the staff role or its permissions.

Figures.Title: Member Welcome Dialog
Figures.Caption: Figure 48. Member Welcome Dialog
Figures.Description: The welcome dialog introduces the member attendance workflow and instructs the member to show the personal QR at the gym for check-in and check-out. Got it dismisses the introductory dialog.

Figures.Title: Member Dashboard Header
Figures.Caption: Figure 49. Member Dashboard Header
Figures.Description: The member dashboard header identifies the signed-in member and provides Show QR Code. The displayed membership state belongs to the captured account.

Figures.Title: Member Attendance QR
Figures.Caption: Figure 50. Member Attendance QR
Figures.Description: The personal QR dialog provides Close and Print actions for presenting the code at the gym. Authorized attendance scanning records the visit; displaying or printing the code alone does not check the member in.

Figures.Title: Membership Progress and Own Attendance
Figures.Caption: Figure 51. Membership Progress and Own Attendance
Figures.Description: The dashboard shows membership duration, remaining time, elapsed progress, and the member's own attendance panel. Membership progress represents elapsed plan time rather than physical fitness improvement.

Figures.Title: Member Renewal Request
Figures.Caption: Figure 52. Member Renewal Request
Figures.Description: The renewal panel displays the member name, plan choice, and Submit Renewal Request. The on-screen explanation describes adding the approved duration after the current expiry for an active membership. Request submission is separate from approval and payment recording.

Figures.Title: Member In-store Product Catalog
Figures.Caption: Figure 53. Member In-store Product Catalog
Figures.Description: The supplied catalog presents supplements and merchandise with images, prices, units, and availability. It supports browsing products for gym purchases without showing an online checkout.

Figures.Title: Member Personal Information
Figures.Caption: Figure 54. Member Personal Information
Figures.Description: The Member Menu displays the member's own name, birth date, and related personal inputs. Its tabs separate personal details, emergency contact, health and fitness, login email, and password.

Figures.Title: Member Personal Information Continuation
Figures.Caption: Figure 55. Member Personal Information Continuation
Figures.Description: The supplied continuation shows age, sex, mobile contact, height, weight, and Save Information. This figure complements the preceding personal-information view and does not expose other members' profiles.

Figures.Title: Member Emergency Contact
Figures.Caption: Figure 56. Member Emergency Contact
Figures.Description: The Emergency Contact tab provides contact name, relationship, number, and Save Information. The member maintains the emergency contact associated with their own record.

Figures.Title: Member Health and Fitness Information
Figures.Caption: Figure 57. Member Health and Fitness Information
Figures.Description: The Health and Fitness tab shows goals and health-declaration selections with a save action. These entries record member-provided information rather than a medical diagnosis or measured fitness outcome.

Figures.Title: Member Login Email Update
Figures.Caption: Figure 58. Member Login Email Update
Figures.Description: The Login Email tab displays the email input and Update Email. Updating authentication details is a separate account action from saving the personal-information form.

Figures.Title: Member Password Update
Figures.Caption: Figure 59. Member Password Update
Figures.Description: The Change Password tab provides new-password and confirmation inputs and Update Password. The visible guidance describes the password requirements and matching confirmation.

Figures.Title: Member Logout Confirmation
Figures.Caption: Figure 60. Member Logout Confirmation
Figures.Description: The member logout dialog offers Cancel and Log out. It confirms the session action before returning the user to the appropriate signed-out state.

Figures.Title: Member Browser Approval Request
Figures.Caption: Figure 61. Member Browser Approval Request
Figures.Description: The Is this you? dialog reports a new browser request, browser details, and request time with Deny and Approve device. The member should approve only a sign-in they initiated; this capture shows a decision prompt rather than its result.

Figures.Title: Member Session Open on Another Device
Figures.Caption: Figure 62. Member Session Open on Another Device
Figures.Description: The sign-in capture displays a message that the member session is open on another device and directs the user to sign out there to continue. This documents the visible session-conflict response rather than a completed browser transfer.
